dialog.body: Utilities Division, this is Tony. How can I help you?
Hi, yes. My name is Adriana Ortiz. I'm calling for my mother, she's the one renting at 479 Harrison Avenue, over on the Fort Adams side.
Okay, Ms. Ortiz. What's going on with the account?

Well, the landlord is telling my mother she owes the water and sewer bill. And I have the bill here, hold on, let me find my place. [pause] Okay. It says the account is in the name of the property owner. So I'd like to know whose bill this is. Because she's a tenant.

Sure, I can explain that. In Newport the water account is generally tied to the property, so the bill goes to the owner on record. Whether a tenant pays it comes down to the lease. Some leases say the tenant reimburses the landlord, some say water is included in the rent. Does your mother's lease mention water?

I don't think so. I mean, I haven't read the whole thing. She has it somewhere. But the landlord just sent a note saying she owes, and the amount is, um, here, it says current charges, and then a previous balance, and then a total. It's a lot more than I'd expect for one woman living alone.
Right. Do you see a line for the meter reading, current and previous?
Yes, it says current read, and next to it there's the letter E. Then previous read.
That E usually means estimated. So nobody got an actual reading, the system guessed based on past use.
That's what I figured. The meter is in a crawlspace under the house and nobody goes in there. My mother certainly doesn't, and the landlord, I doubt he does either. So how would anybody read it?

Well, that's the problem with those. If the meter's hard to get to, we can end up estimating several bills in a row, and then a real reading comes along and catches up. I can note the account that the meter is in a crawlspace and have someone look at whether there's a remote reader or if an appointment is needed.
Please do. Because honestly it's ridiculous to be handed a bill based on a guess and told it's my mother's problem. I'm not paying a guess.

Understood. Now, the dispute with the landlord about who owes it, that's between the two of them, I can't settle that. But I can tell you the bill itself should be based on a real reading, and I can flag it. The owner is the one who'd have to request the check, since it's his account. Do you have his contact info, or can your mother ask him?
She can ask him. He's not hard to reach, he just doesn't like to be asked. I'll make him. Can I give you my number in case someone needs to call about it?
Sure, go ahead.
Got it, 401-555-0163. I'll put that on the note along with the crawlspace.

Thank you. Now, one more thing. If somebody does end up having to pay this, can I do it on the website with a card? Right now, I mean, it's already afternoon, and I don't know if it only works during office hours or if it's open late.

The website's up all the time, so you can pay with a card there any hour, evenings and weekends included. It's not tied to when City Hall is open. There's also a drop box for checks if you'd rather do that.
Okay, good. I'm not paying yet, though. I want the reading first.
That makes sense. I'd get the owner to request that check first.

I will. Sorry, I'm a little short today. I've had this thing in my hand since breakfast and I keep getting interrupted by the television. I've been watching this cooking show all week, the one with the baking competition, and it's on in the other room.
No worries at all. Anything else I can look up for you?
No, that's it. Just the crawlspace and the estimate. Don't forget.
It's going on the account right now. Take care, Ms. Ortiz.
Thank you. Goodbye.
